task_kinds.metric: Verified automatically from git/chat metrics by `coach.py verify`. Cannot be self-marked.
task_kinds.attest: Done when the developer supplies evidence (commit, PR, file). The coach challenges thin evidence.
task_kinds.quiz: Done when the developer passes an in-session check without AI help. Quiz-kind tasks are re-tested on a spaced schedule (+3, +10, +30 days).

change-hygiene.title: Change hygiene: small, reviewable, reversible changes
change-hygiene.senior_looks_like: One concern per change. Commits say why. PRs are small enough to review in one sitting and revert without collateral damage. CI is green before 'done'.
change-hygiene.why: When you are your own reviewer (solo, or leaning on AI), sprawling diffs are where auth and data bugs hide.

tasks.title: What vs why in commit messages
tasks.do: Rewrite your last 10 vague subjects as `type(scope): why`. Then answer: which of your commits could a stranger revert safely, and why?

tasks.title: Write the split plan for your biggest change
tasks.do: Take {largest_commit}. Write 3-5 slices, each independently revertable, each with its own test. Paste the plan as evidence.

tasks.title: Land 10 commits that meet the bar
tasks.do: Ten consecutive commits: conventional format, median files per commit at or under the cap.

tasks.title: Ship one small, well-described PR
tasks.do: One PR under ~400 changed lines with what / why / risk / test plan / rollback in the description. Evidence: PR URL or commit range.

modular-architecture.title: Modular architecture under growth
modular-architecture.senior_looks_like: Clear boundaries (UI shell / domain service / API / authorization). Hotspots shrink over time. Nobody accepts a multi-thousand-line file as its permanent home.
modular-architecture.why: God files become untestable, and they are hostile to AI tools too: oversized context produces worse generated code.

tasks.title: Deep vs shallow modules, applied to your code
tasks.do: For {god_file_1}: list its distinct responsibilities, then sketch the module map you would draw if it were new. Quiz: why does a thin interface over deep logic beat many tiny pass-through functions?

tasks.title: Pin behavior before you split
tasks.do: Write characterization tests around the part of {god_file_1} you will extract. Evidence: test file + passing run.

tasks.title: Extract one module, no behavior change
tasks.do: One PR that only moves code out of {god_file_1}. Evidence: PR/commit range showing tests unchanged and green.

tasks.title: Make the hotspot measurably smaller
tasks.do: Top baseline god files lose at least 20% of their lines (or are split).

test-as-gate.title: Tests as a gate, not an afterthought
test-as-gate.senior_looks_like: The riskiest paths are tested in the same change that touches them. A red CI blocks the merge; it is not 'informative'.
test-as-gate.why: In multi-tenant or money-handling software, the expensive bugs are wrong-scope and wrong-permission bugs, which tests catch cheaply.

tasks.title: Risk-based test selection
tasks.do: For a typical new API route define the minimum trio: permission denied, happy path, wrong-scope (other tenant/org) miss. Quiz: which of the three catches the most expensive bug, and why?

tasks.title: Write the trio for one existing route
tasks.do: Pick {risky_path_1} (or another risky route). Add the three tests. Evidence: commit hash.

tasks.title: Ten source commits, tests alongside
tasks.do: At least 70% of your next 10+ source-touching commits include test changes.

tasks.title: Make test prerequisites fail fast
tasks.do: Browsers/fixtures/env needed by e2e tests are checked up front (script, CI step or onboarding doc). Evidence: the change.

ai-ownership.title: Owning AI-generated changes
ai-ownership.senior_looks_like: AI proposes, you decide. You can delete 30% of an AI diff and the feature still works. Every AI change gets the review you would give a new junior's PR.
ai-ownership.why: High AI throughput without ownership turns you into a prompt operator and multiplies debt in places you cannot explain.

tasks.title: Write a prompt contract
tasks.do: For your next AI task write: goal, non-goals, allowed files, forbidden files, acceptance criteria, required tests, max scope. Evidence: the prompt text.

tasks.title: Blast-radius note for a past AI change
tasks.do: Pick a recent AI-heavy PR. Write 5 bullets: callers, auth, data, UI, rollback. Log with `coach.py note --kind blast-radius`.

tasks.title: Five AI changes, five notes
tasks.do: Log a blast-radius note before merging each of five AI-assisted changes.

tasks.title: Explain it without the chat
tasks.do: The coach picks a large AI-authored change from your history. Explain end to end, with no AI open: what it does, where it can break, how you would roll it back.

tasks.title: Four no-agent weeks (small fix each)
tasks.do: Once a week implement one small fix without generation tools. Evidence: four commit hashes.

operational-predictability.title: Operational predictability
operational-predictability.senior_looks_like: Known failure classes are prevented by checklists and CI contracts, not remembered. 'Merged' is not 'done' until the user path is smoke-tested.
operational-predictability.why: Repeat failures (broken CI prerequisites, merged-but-wrong features, reverts) are process bugs, not bad luck.

tasks.title: Turn incidents into checklist items
tasks.do: List your last 5 'that should not have happened' moments. For each: the class of failure and the one-line check that would have prevented it.

tasks.title: Install the hooks and CI backstop
tasks.do: Run `coach.py install-hooks` and add the GitHub Action from integrations/.

tasks.title: PR template with the checklist
tasks.do: Add .github/pull_request_template.md covering permissions, org scope, tests, schema/migrations, secrets, UI smoke path.

tasks.title: Smoke the user path on three features
tasks.do: For three features, write the smoke path in the PR and tick it after merge. Evidence: 3 PR links.

security-hygiene.title: Security and data-handling hygiene
security-hygiene.senior_looks_like: Secrets never land in history. Every authorization-relevant change ships with deny and scope tests. Policy is audited, not assumed.
security-hygiene.why: Intent without process still leaks: secrets in history and untested permission paths are the usual failures.

tasks.title: Threat-model one route
tasks.do: Pick {risky_path_1}. Who can call it, what can they reach, what if the tenant/org id is forged? Quiz on three abuse cases.

tasks.title: Rotate, scan, prevent
tasks.do: Rotate anything that ever leaked. Enable the pre-commit scan (coach hooks or a dedicated scanner). Evidence: config commit.

tasks.title: Risky changes ship with tests
tasks.do: Five+ commits touching auth/permission/tenant/billing paths, at least 80% with tests.

tasks.title: Monthly audit of 10 routes
tasks.do: Audit 10 routes against your own authorization rules. Evidence: the checklist with findings.

debugging-method.title: Hypothesis-driven debugging
debugging-method.senior_looks_like: Observe, hypothesize, predict, test, record. Every fix leaves behind a regression test and a root-cause sentence.
debugging-method.why: Fix-after-fix chains and pasted errors without a hypothesis mean the cause was never isolated.

tasks.title: The hypothesis loop
tasks.do: Given a bug report the coach provides, produce ranked hypotheses and the cheapest experiment for each before touching code.

tasks.title: Debug log for the next three bugs
tasks.do: Symptom, ranked hypotheses, experiment, root cause, regression test. Evidence: three logs.

tasks.title: Every fix ships a regression test
tasks.do: Five+ fix commits, at least 80% with tests.

tasks.title: Five whys on a fix-after-fix chain
tasks.do: Take a chain where a fix needed a follow-up fix. Trace to the process cause. Evidence: written analysis.

requirements-clarity.title: Requirements and prompt clarity
requirements-clarity.senior_looks_like: Work starts from constraints, non-goals and acceptance criteria, so anyone (human or AI) can tell when it is done.
requirements-clarity.why: Vague asks produce broad diffs and fix-after-ship loops.

tasks.title: Acceptance criteria and non-goals
tasks.do: Turn a one-line feature wish from your backlog into Given/When/Then plus explicit non-goals.

tasks.title: Rewrite three vague prompts
tasks.do: Take three vague prompts from your chat sample and rewrite them as contracts. Evidence: before/after.

tasks.title: Ten prompts with constraints
tasks.do: Re-run `coach.py verify --chat PATH` after ten new substantial prompts.

retrieval-quiz.name: Retrieval quiz
retrieval-quiz.fits: Concepts and judgment calls the developer must apply from memory

worked-example.name: Worked example, then faded
worked-example.fits: A skill the developer has not done before; agent demonstrates on a different case, developer does their own

guided-refactor.name: Guided refactor on your own code
guided-refactor.fits: Structure and architecture gaps; developer drives, agent navigates and asks questions

deliberate-kata.name: Deliberate-practice kata
deliberate-kata.fits: Small repeatable habits (messages, tests, fixes); repeat 3x with feedback each round

review-drill.name: Seeded-flaw review drill
review-drill.fits: Spotting risk in diffs, routes or plans; agent plants or selects flaws, developer finds them

debug-lab.name: Debugging lab
debug-lab.fits: Hypothesis-driven debugging; agent provides a bug case, developer runs the loop

explain-back.name: Explain-back
explain-back.fits: Ownership of AI-written or old code; developer explains it with no AI open, graded on a rubric

pre-mortem.name: Pre-mortem and checklist building
pre-mortem.fits: Process and reliability gaps; turn likely failures into checks

if-then-plan.name: If-then plan tied to a live trigger
if-then-plan.fits: Habit gaps; developer writes 'when X happens I do Y', hooks supply the trigger

rewrite-artifact.name: Before/after rewrite of your own artifact
rewrite-artifact.fits: Communication gaps in commits, prompts, tickets, PR text

design-note.name: Short design note (ADR)
design-note.fits: Boundary and trade-off decisions; one page: context, options, decision, consequences

live-pairing.name: Live pairing on a real backlog item
live-pairing.fits: Applying a skill under real constraints; agent enforces the constraints during the work

metric-challenge.name: Metric challenge
metric-challenge.fits: Behavior change that git or chat can measure; verified automatically
